transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me?

Hi, thank you. Um, I came in today because I keep having these evenings where I just eat a really large amount of food. I'll buy a whole family-size takeout order, and then I usually add chips or bakery things from the grocery store. And I end up eating most of it myself. It's like I don't even really register how much is gone until I've already eaten it all.

After one of these episodes where you eat a large amount, do you ever try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting the next day, or exercising a lot more than usual?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or anything. I don't really exercise much to begin with, so I definitely don't do that to make up for it. And I don't skip meals the next day either. I just... I just eat it and that's it.
During these episodes, do you feel a sense of being out of control—like you can't stop eating even if you want to—and do you feel upset, guilty, or distressed about it afterward?

Yes, that's exactly it. Once I start, there is this awful switch that flips. I can actually be thinking to myself, Taylor, put it away, but my hands just keep opening containers anyway. It's like I am not the one in charge. And then afterward... yes, I feel incredibly guilty and upset about the whole thing.
Over the past three months, about how many times per week have you had these large binge-eating episodes?

Um, well, I actually keep a journal. And when I look back through it, there has barely been a single week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. Honestly, most weeks, it happens several times.

latest_inference.note: Frequency (several times/week for months), loss of control, and marked distress confirm binge-eating pattern; absence of compensatory behaviors rules out bulimia nervosa, solidifying binge-eating disorder (coded under F50.8) as the diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food with a subjective sense of loss of control, occurring multiple times per week for several months, followed by marked guilt and distress. There are no compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or excessive exercise, ruling out bulimia nervosa (F50.2). This pattern is consistent with Binge Eating Disorder, which in ICD-10 is coded under 'Other eating disorders' (F50.8) since there is no dedicated BED code in this classification system.

confirmed_symptoms: Eating an objectively large amount of food (family-size meal plus additional snacks) in a discrete period
Sense of loss of control during eating ('the switch flips', 'not the one in charge')
Eating rapidly/until food is gone without full awareness of quantity consumed
Marked guilt and distress after episodes

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Binge episodes occurring at least once weekly, often several times per week, over the past several months (per patient's journal tracking)
additional_requirements: Frequency criterion (at least weekly) established via patient's self-monitoring journal
